nodes.body:
@sepo-agent /answer 

Review the latest github activities (see existing issues, prs, and discussion (ideas)) and triage the most important tasks to do ?

I’d triage the latest activity this way:

**Do first**

1. **Close the self-approval safety gap: #224.** This is the highest-risk open task because it protects a privileged path. Before relying on self-approval/self-merge, Sepo should block approval when the PR author is also the initiating requester, not only when the approval token actor matches the PR author.

2. **Finish the fresh simplified self-merge path: #229 under #170.** Most self-approval PRs have now merged, and the older self-merge attempts #202/#214 were closed. The active path should stay small: opt-in `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_MERGE`, trusted current-head Sepo approval, no blocking requested changes, checks/mergeability, and `--match-head-commit`.

3. **Land or minimally adjust #221.** The shared route catalog PR is the right fix for route drift, and review already said `SHIP`. I would address the maintainer’s “make it minimal” feedback, keep `.agent/src/routes.ts` as the semantic source of truth, then mark ready/merge. This also helps future route work like `/publish-failure-report`, `/orchestrate`, and better `/implement` handling.

**Do next**

4. **Fix the `/implement` PR-origin UX: #228 and the real gap from #227.** #228 is low-effort: derive a better tracking issue title from the explicit `/implement` request instead of always using “Implement requested change.” #227 clarified that PR/discussion `/implement` dispatch exists, but PR-origin `/implement` does not automatically stack on the current PR. That should become a focused follow-up after #221.

5. **Decide what to do with large draft PR #158.** It implements approval-gated failure diagnosis/reporting and has passed checks, but it is broad and stale. I’d either review/merge it deliberately or split it; leaving it open will keep creating planning noise.

6. **Revisit app installation automation #119 / distribution #107.** This remains important for post-v0.1.0 adoption, but it is less urgent than the privileged self-approval/self-merge safety path. The repo-side pieces exist conceptually; the hosted App webhook/bootstrap boundary is the key remaining product decision.

**Do later / design first**

7. **Promote the new research/orchestrator ideas into explicit design issues before coding.** Discussions #223, #225, and #226 all point at the same architectural direction: Sepo needs strategy-specific orchestration state, not just a smarter prompt. Current orchestrator behavior is still a bounded single-next-action model: [`AgentAction`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L3), one validated planner decision, and sequential child reporting through [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L990-L1057). Parallel/best-of-n/research loops need batch state, reducers, budgets, and structured result payloads first.

My recommended execution order:

1. #224  
2. #229  
3. #221  
4. #228 plus PR-origin stacking follow-up from #227  
5. #158 decision  
6. #119/#107 install/distribution work  
7. Convert #223/#225/#226 into a phased strategy/experiment design track

I would not start the auto-research or parallel-orchestrator work until the self-approval/self-merge privilege boundary and route catalog are stable. Those are the foundations the newer ideas depend on.
